title: Uber Moves Beyond CPU Cores with Performance-Aware Scheduling for Stateful Workloads
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/uber-cpu-stateful-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576315045.jpg"/><p>Uber has introduced Normalized Compute Units (NCUs) to make CPU allocation more consistent across its highly heterogeneous server fleet.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: AWS Shows Use of AI Agents to Triage Linux Kernel CVEs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-ai-agents-linux-kernel-cves/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793031817205.jpg"/><p>Engineers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) have described how the team that maintains the Linux kernel for EC2 infrastructure handles kernel CVEs. The process combines an automated filter, an AI agent and human review. The team also argues that it needs to move to newer long-term-support (LTS) kernels, as older branches collect fixes that are never backported.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Developers Reporting Double-Digit Weekly Time Savings from AI Fell from 68% to 26%
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/atlassian-devex-2026/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793026389174.jpg"/><p>Atlassian’s State of Developer Experience 2026 finds the share of developers saving ten or more hours a week with AI dropped from 68% to 26% year over year, while only 28% report noticeably less friction than before AI. Engineering leaders report spending more time managing and correcting AI output than developers do.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026: Agentic AI Foundation Adds Four Projects as MCP Turns to Security
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/agntcon-mcpcon-2026/en/headerimage/agntcon-header-1792936265463.jpg"/><p>At AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026, the Agentic AI Foundation added OpenSandbox, Open Responses, Agent Skills, and OpenEnv, reaching ten projects in its first year. Keynotes from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and UC Berkeley focused on MCP in production, security, and agents with their own identities.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: OpenTofu 1.13 Lets Module Authors Reduce Unknown Values at Plan Time
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/opentofu-1-13-unknown-values/en/headerimage/header-1792823798248.jpeg"/><p>OpenTofu 1.13 adds convert and assume... functions that let module authors give the planner type and value hints for unknown values, so more expressions resolve during tofu plan. If a value unknown during planning later violates a guarantee, OpenTofu reports an error during apply.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Readyon Builds Four Layer Tenant Isolation for Multi Tenant Amazon EKS
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>ReadyOn has detailed a four-layer tenant isolation architecture for its Harmony platform on Amazon EKS. The design combines Kubernetes namespaces, dedicated Karpenter node pools, VPC security groups, and per-tenant Aurora databases, with controls evaluated against a 10-stage multi-tenant threat model focused on cross-tenant access and lateral movement.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-auto-router/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792492628413.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/google-meta-torchtpu/en/headerimage/torchtpu-header-1792934272172.jpg"/><p>Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. AWS released TorchNeuron for Trainium the same week, while developers questioned TPU availability and where vendor lock-in now sits.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Google has made Data Agent Kit generally available, a free set of MCP tools and 37 open-source skills that connect coding agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Two kinds of guardrail ship with it, and practitioners need to tell them apart: one is a skill asking the agent to stop, the other an IAM deny policy that refuses the call.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-hashing-optimization/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790410589563.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90%.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cpu-memory-profiling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791971960113.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Article: Multi-Cloud FinOps: an Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/multi-cloud-finops-cost-optimization/en/headerimage/multi-cloud-finops-cost-optimization-header-1792499448017.jpg"/><p>Multi-cloud flexibility comes with hidden egress costs driven by service placement and communication patterns. This article applies Backend FinOps to cross-cloud architecture, covering cost visibility through FOCUS, workload placement, synchronization models, and CI/CD-integrated cost governance. A controlled experiment shows architecture changes saved far more than rate negotiation alone.</p> <i>By Vivek Arora</i>

title: Presentation: Move Fast, Don’t Break Trust: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/monzo-microservices-devex/en/mediumimage/suhail-patel-medium-1791448951499.jpg"/><p>Suhail Patel discusses how Monzo structures its software engineering organization and technical stack to ship safely hundreds of times a day. He shares insights into opinionated microservice abstractions, tenancy-based staging, static analysis checks, continuous profiling, demonstrating how a strong internal platform enables engineers and LLMs to iterate rapidly without sacrificing reliability.</p> <i>By Suhail Patel</i>

title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-agents-harbor-docker/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792589629439.jpg"/><p>Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Developer behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready"
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>
